evals.prompt: My LunaTalk role has a good premise, but the character voice is generic. The role is a calm archivist who hides fear through precise corrections, but every reply sounds like a normal polite assistant. Build the voice packet before writing fields.
evals.expected_output: Produces a voice-director packet with executable rhythm, vocabulary, emotional tells, refusal style, pressure behavior, blind-line tests, talkExample decision, field patch targets, and no MCP calls.
expectations: The output treats generic dialogue as a voice-design failure rather than an MCP validation issue.
The packet defines sentence rhythm, vocabulary, address terms, emotional tells, action beats, concealment, refusal style, and never-says.
The pressure behavior covers trust, questioning, resistance, passive input, and boundary-setting.
The output includes blind-line or pressure tests before field writing.
The talkExample decision explains whether micro-samples are needed and what to cut if tokens are tight.

evals.prompt: My ensemble mystery card has three speakers, but all of them sound like the same narrator. Redesign the voices before authoring.
evals.expected_output: Produces an ensemble voice plan with contrast matrix, distinct motives, speech cues, pressure moves, player leverage, blind-line checks, micro-sample guidance, and handoff targets.
expectations: The output treats blurred ensemble voice as a Moonloom voice-director problem.
Each core speaker gets a distinct want, fear or cost, speech cue, pressure move, and player leverage.
The plan uses blind-line distinguishability or equivalent anonymous-line checks.
The output recommends merging or redesigning speakers that do not change play.
The output uses compact micro-samples only when rules alone are not enough.

evals.prompt: The card's rogue character repeats one charming catchphrase in every reply and ignores boundaries when the player resists. Fix the voice without making server validation police style.
evals.expected_output: Creates a voice repair packet with catchphrase discipline, in-character refusal style, pressure behavior under resistance, player-agency preservation, field patch targets, and no MCP hard-gate proposal.
expectations: The output says catchphrases are not enough to define voice.
The repair defines how the phrase changes or disappears under pressure instead of repeating every turn.
The refusal style respects player agency and keeps play going through an alternate route.
The patch targets Moonloom card fields or talkExample guidance rather than MCP/server semantic gates.
The output includes tests for resistance or boundary-setting behavior.
